title: SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Falls 6.4% as Tech Stocks Slide (Oct 30)
summary: SpaceX (SPCX) fell 6.37% to $134.72 on Oct. 30 as a tech selloff deepened, closing near its day low and just under its $135 IPO price.
body_markdown:
## Why SpaceX Stock Fell


Financial media coverage of the October 30 session named no SpaceX-specific news behind the drop. Instead, according to[the Associated Press](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/10/30/sell-off-for-tech-stocks-worsens-and-drowns-out-strength-elsewhere-on-wall-street/) , the sell-off for tech stocks deepened as worries rose about whether hundreds of billions of dollars of AI spending "will produce enough profit and productivity." AP added that[Intel's forecast](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/intel-plunges-21-on-weak-pc-guidance-chip-stocks-sell-off/) for the final quarter of 2026 fell well short, and that chip stocks and other AI data-center beneficiaries fell on fears that high interest rates may slow data-center buildouts.


SpaceX's own numbers show how large its AI business has become. According to its[quarterly report on Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/spcx-20260930.htm) , the Super Intelligence segment brought in $7,560 million of total third-quarter revenue of $14,575 million, up from $813 million a year earlier. Motley Fool describes that unit as renting computing power and selling AI software and ads.


Financial media did not tie Friday's drop to that exposure directly. A[Motley Fool column](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/spacex-stock-nearly-30-below-200301582.html) published after the session said "the doubt is whether the AI spending pays off," and noted that SpaceX[went public](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) in June at $135 per share, just above Friday's close.


## SPCX Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Third-quarter revenue rose to $14,575 million from $5,576 million a year earlier, according to the 10-Q, with the Connectivity segment growing to $5,248 million from $3,097 million.
- Starlink reached 13.6 million consumer subscribers at the end of September, up about 89% from a year earlier, as reported by[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/starlinks-subscriber-growth-explosive-could-212200816.html) , citing SpaceX's filings.
- Management expects first-quarter 2027 revenue of $33 billion to $37 billion, per Motley Fool.


### Risks


- Purchases of property, plant and equipment reached $48,069 million in the first nine months of 2026, up from $13,846 million a year earlier, per the 10-Q. Motley Fool set that spending against $13.1 billion of operating cash flow.
- Elon Musk said SpaceX rents computing power at "effectively the spot-market rate," so revenue may swing with rental prices, according to Motley Fool. Starlink's average revenue per user also fell to $69 in the third quarter from $83 a year earlier.
- [Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spacex-spcx-loses-bid-dismiss-131232322.html) reported on November 1 that a federal judge let an NAACP Clean Air Act complaint over gas-fired turbine emissions at SpaceX's Mississippi AI data centers proceed.
- Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter call that merging with Tesla was a good idea, and each company formed a special committee.[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/barclays-says-spacex-merger-now-210500947.html) flagged heavy dilution for SpaceX holders if a deal is paid in stock.


This article is for education and information only and is not investment advice. Investment decisions are yours to make after your own research.
